sources.entry: PPRows - Application to calculate how many lines of code you write. ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/jkpang/PPRows)

summary.one_liner: PPRows is a macOS app that counts lines of code in files and folders you drag onto its window.
summary.what_it_does: The README says PPRows counts how many lines of code you have written on a Mac. You drag files or folders onto the app window, and it reports the number of code folders involved and the number of lines. It can process several files or folders at once. File types are customizable, with examples given as C, Swift, Objective-C and Java. Folders can be excluded from the count, such as a Pods folder in an iOS project. From v1.2.0, empty lines can be ignored for a more accurate count. The interface supports Chinese and English and follows the system language.
use_cases: count lines of code in a project
measure how much code you have written
count code in an iOS or Xcode project
exclude dependency folders like Pods from line counts
count lines across multiple code folders at once
how_to_run: Drag file / folder to the PPRows App window.
notable: Drag-and-drop input for files and folders
Customizable file-type filter (C, Swift, Objective-C, Java, and others)
Folder exclusion list for directories such as Pods
Chinese and English interface that follows system language (v1.1.0)
caveats: Requires Mac OS X 10.11 or later and Xcode 8 or later
The App Store version is paid (the README gives $0.5), and the README says the code can be used free of charge
The README has no description of how the source code is built
keywords: how much code did i write
